content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E24","hypothesis_id":"H04","title":"Single-omission matrix for donor-linked cobalt-state effects","purpose":"Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables and CO/H2 distribution requires the full CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 assembly, using explicit one-factor omissions and bounded background interpretation.","evidence_ids":["EV059","GX016","GX008","EV081"],"source_to_proposal":"EV059 supports the CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4+TEOA formulation family in MeCN/H2O and motivates this as the closest source-anchored platform for donor comparison. GX008 supports explicit negative controls and paired characterization plus product analysis. EV081 shows that partial or no-catalyst systems can still produce CO and H2, so omission results must be treated as necessity/background tests rather than proof of mechanism. GX016 supports the transferable idea that cobalt-centered identity can shift product selectivity under TEOA photocatalysis, motivating tests of whether donor-linked effects persist or collapse when ligand or support is removed. The proposal transfers these observations into a controlled omission matrix in the P01-style system; it does not assume literature-established active-species identity or that omitted formulations are do not infer a single active species from one spectroscopic signature or recovered samples alone."],"measurements":["CO and H2 quantified together by one matched GC workflow for all groups, reporting amount and CO/H2 distribution.","A cobalt-state observable from an element- or coordination-sensitive method feasible in the laboratory context, such as operando or near-operando XAS, XPS-compatible sampling, or UV-Vis features, with sample state stated explicitly.","Change in cobalt-related spectral features or signal intensity from pre-illumination to illuminated CO2 conditions as a bounded indicator of donor-linked state change or deactivation.","Background product formation in omission groups, used to bound non-full-assembly contributions rather than to claim catalytic equivalence."],"supports":"H04 is supported if the full assembly shows a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables or stability trends and that donor-linked difference weakens, disappears, or changes character in at least one omission pair, indicating dependence on ligand or support context. Stronger support occurs if the direction of cobalt-state differences tracks the direction of CO/H2 changes across matched pairs.","refutes":"H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable cobalt-state and stability observables in the full assembly within method resolution, and the ligand-omission and support-omission donor pairs likewise show no reproducible donor-linked divergence despite measurable products. It is further weakened if donor substitution changes CO/H2 but cobalt-state observables remain unchanged across all matched formulations.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if product signals are near background, cobalt-state signals are below detection or assignment is non-unique, omission causes optical or compositional changes that prevent comparable measurements, or session-to-session drift obscures donor-pair comparisons. A change seen in only one method without corroboration remains provisional.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent concentrations, catalyst loadings, or illumination settings. Use the verified EV059-style baseline for starting composition, then perform a pilot to choose the lowest concentration and path length that still provide stable cobalt-state signal above blanks and measurable CO and H2 above analytical detection. Choose an early sampling window before heavy conversion or visible precipitation. If support omission changes turbidity or absorbance, recalibrate acquisition settings with blanks while keeping reactor geometry, gas handling, and timing identical across compared groups.","limitations":"Omission of bpy or g-C3N4 may generate qualitatively different cobalt species rather than partial versions of the full catalyst, so these are dependence tests, not continuity proofs. EV059 does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one frozen recipe, so baseline comparability still requires verification. Recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state, and generic spectral changes cannot by themselves identify the active species or exact coordination geometry.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
